verse: It is of the LORD’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.
title: Mercy With Your Name on It
message: Jeremiah wrote these words while sitting in the ruins of Jerusalem. Everything familiar was gone. And yet, in the middle of the rubble, he remembered one thing that had not been destroyed: the mercy of God.
Yesterday’s mistakes do not get the last word over today. God did not wake up tired of you. His compassion was waiting for you before your eyes opened this morning. Receive it fresh, and begin again.
prayer: Faithful God, thank You for mercy that is new this morning. I receive it, and I begin again with You.

verse: Be still, and know that I am God.
title: Stop, and Know
message: The Hebrew word behind “be still” carries the idea of letting go, of dropping your hands. It was written for people surrounded by roaring nations and shaking mountains.

Stillness is not doing nothing. It is choosing to stop striving long enough to remember who is in charge. Before you reach for your phone, your plans or your worries today, pause. Breathe. Know that He is God, and you are not, and that is very good news.
prayer: Lord, I drop my hands. Quiet my heart until I know again that You are God.

verse: Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
title: Five Promises for a Fearful Heart
message: Count the promises in this one verse: I am with thee. I am thy God. I will strengthen thee. I will help thee. I will uphold thee.

God doesn’t answer fear with a lecture. He answers it with His presence. Whatever you are facing today, you will not face it alone or in your own strength. The same right hand that stretched out the heavens is holding you up right now.
prayer: Father, when fear speaks today, remind me that You are with me, helping me and holding me.

verse: Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
title: When You Can’t See the Whole Road
message: We like to understand before we trust. God often asks us to trust before we understand. “Lean not” paints the picture of someone putting their full weight on a walking stick that cannot hold them.

Your understanding is a good gift, but it is too small to carry your whole life. Acknowledge Him in the small decisions today: the conversation, the errand, the reply. He is faithful to direct the steps of those who invite Him in.
prayer: Lord, I lean on You, not on my own understanding. Direct my steps today.

verse: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
title: An Invitation for the Tired
message: Jesus didn’t say, “Come to Me once you’ve got it together.” He invited the laboring and the heavy laden. The tired. The overwhelmed. The ones carrying more than they can hold.

Rest isn’t first a place or a vacation. It’s a Person. You can bring Him the weight you’re carrying today, the list, the worry, the grief, and trade it for His easy yoke. He is gentle and lowly in heart. Come.
prayer: Jesus, I’m coming to You tired. Thank You for rest that only You can give.

verse: I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
title: Strength for Every Season
message: Paul wrote this from a prison cell. Just before it, he says he has learned to be content whether full or hungry, with plenty or in need. This verse isn’t about winning every game; it’s about enduring every season.
Whatever today holds, abundance or lack, joy or loss, Christ will supply the strength to walk through it faithfully. You don’t need tomorrow’s strength yet. You only need today’s, and He gives it.
prayer: Christ, be my strength for exactly what today holds.

verse: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
title: Led by a Good Shepherd
message: David had been a shepherd. He knew sheep don’t find green pastures by accident. They are led. They are protected. They are counted when one goes missing.

To say “The LORD is my shepherd” is to admit you’re a sheep: you need guidance, care and rescue. That isn’t weakness; it’s freedom. You don’t have to carry the responsibility of leading yourself today. Follow the One who knows the way to still waters.
prayer: Good Shepherd, lead me today. I trust You to provide everything I truly need.

verse: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.
title: Nothing Wasted
message: This verse doesn’t say all things are good. Loss isn’t good. Betrayal isn’t good. Sickness isn’t good. It says God works all things together for good, like a master weaver using even the dark threads.

You may not see the pattern today. That’s all right. The One holding the loom is wise and kind, and He wastes nothing in the life of someone who loves Him. Hand Him today’s threads, even the painful ones.
prayer: Father, I don’t understand everything, but I trust You to weave it all for good.

verse: Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the LORD thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.
title: Courage Has a Reason
message: Joshua was stepping into Moses’ shoes, leading a nation into a land full of giants. God told him three times to be strong and courageous, and the last time He gave the deepest reason of all: I am with you.
Courage isn’t pretending you’re not afraid. It’s remembering who walks into the room with you. Wherever you go today, the hospital, the office, the hard conversation, God is already there.
prayer: Lord, You are with me wherever I go. Give me courage for the step in front of me.

verse: But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.
title: Strength for Ordinary Days
message: Notice the order: soar, run, walk. We expect God to help us most in the dramatic moments, but the greatest miracle may be the last one: walking and not fainting.
Most of life is walking. Laundry, commutes, emails, caring for people. Waiting on the Lord means turning to Him again and again in those ordinary hours, and He renews strength for exactly those days.
prayer: Lord, renew my strength today, not just for the big moments, but for the ordinary walk.

verse: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
title: A Different Kind of Peace
message: Jesus spoke these words hours before His arrest. He knew what was coming, and still He gave His friends peace. His peace doesn’t depend on calm circumstances.

The world’s peace says, “Everything will be fine.” Christ’s peace says, “I am with you, even if it isn’t.” That peace is a gift, which means you receive it, you don’t manufacture it. Open your hands for it today.
prayer: Jesus, I receive Your peace. Guard my heart from trouble and fear today.

verse: This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.
title: This Day Is a Gift
message: This psalm was sung by people who had just been rescued. “This is the day” looked back at what God had done, and forward with gratitude.

Today isn’t a random square on a calendar. God made it, and He made it with you in mind. Look for one gift in it: a kind word, warm coffee, a moment of beauty. Rejoicing isn’t ignoring problems; it’s noticing God in the middle of them.
prayer: Thank You, Lord, for this day You made. Open my eyes to Your gifts in it.

verse: Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.
title: You Are Not Who You Were
message: The past has a loud voice. It reminds you of what you did, what was done to you, and who you used to be. But in Christ, there is a new creation.

God doesn’t just patch up the old you; He makes you new. Old things have passed away. When the past tries to define you today, answer it with this verse. Your identity is no longer your history. It’s His work in you.
prayer: Lord, thank You for making me new. Help me live today as the person You say I am.

verse: The LORD thy God in the midst of thee is mighty; he will save, he will rejoice over thee with joy; he will rest in his love, he will joy over thee with singing.
title: God Sings Over You
message: We often picture God tolerating us, frowning at our failures. Zephaniah gives us a stunning picture: God rejoicing over His people with singing, like a parent humming over a sleeping child.
You are not merely put up with. You are delighted in. Let that settle over your heart today. The mighty God, the One who saves, is quiet in His love for you, and glad that you are His.
prayer: Father, help me believe that You delight in me, and let Your love quiet my heart.

verse: The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.
title: Close to the Brokenhearted
message: When your heart is broken, it’s easy to feel that God has moved far away. Scripture says the opposite: He draws near.

You don’t have to hide your tears or pretend to be fine. The Lord is nigh, close enough to hear the prayer you can’t quite say out loud. If today is a heavy day, you are not alone in it. He is closer than you think.
prayer: Lord, my heart is tender. Thank You for drawing near. Hold me close today.

verse: He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?
title: Three Simple Things
message: Sometimes we make following God more complicated than He does. Micah sums it up in three phrases: do what is right, love mercy, and walk humbly with God.
Today, look for one way to be fair, one way to be kind, and one moment to bow your heart. Faithfulness is often small and quiet, and God treasures it.
prayer: Lord, help me do justly, love mercy and walk humbly with You today.

verse: Delight thyself also in the LORD; and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart.
title: Desires Reshaped by Delight
message: This verse isn’t a formula for getting what we want. It’s a promise about what happens when God Himself becomes our greatest joy.

As you delight in Him, He begins to shape your desires to match His heart, and then He loves to fulfill them. Spend a few minutes today simply enjoying God: His Word, His creation, His faithfulness. Let Him become the desire beneath every other desire.
prayer: Lord, be my delight. Shape my desires until they look like Yours.

verse: I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.
title: Never, Ever Alone
message: In the original Greek, this promise stacks negatives on top of each other: I will never, no never, leave you; I will never, no never, forsake you.

People may leave. Seasons change. Friends move away. But God has made a promise He will not break. Whatever loneliness you feel today, this is the truth beneath it: you have never been abandoned by Him, and you never will be.
prayer: Father, thank You that You will never leave me. Let me feel Your nearness today.

verse: And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not.
title: Keep Sowing
message: Farmers don’t plant seeds in the morning and dig them up at night to check progress. Harvest takes time, sometimes longer than we hoped.
Maybe you’ve been praying, serving, loving or parenting faithfully and seeing little fruit. Don’t give up. God has a due season, and no seed planted in faith is lost. Keep sowing today.
prayer: Lord, when I’m weary of doing good, strengthen me to keep sowing until the harvest.

verse: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
title: The Freedom of Confession
message: Shame tells us to hide. Grace invites us to come into the light. Confession isn’t groveling; it’s simply agreeing with God about what is true.

And look at His response: faithful and just to forgive. Not reluctant. Not grudging. Jesus has already paid for every sin you bring. Whatever you’ve been carrying, you can set it down today and walk away clean.
prayer: Lord, I bring You what I’ve been hiding. Thank You for forgiving and cleansing me.

verse: I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works; and that my soul knoweth right well.
title: Wonderfully Made
message: Before anyone ever compared you, critiqued you or overlooked you, God formed you with care. David says he was woven together in secret, seen by God before a single day of his life had begun.
The voice of comparison is loud, but it is not the voice of your Creator. Today, thank God for one thing about how He made you. His works are marvelous, and that includes you.
prayer: Creator God, thank You for making me with care. Help my soul know it well.

verse: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
title: First Things First
message: Jesus spoke these words to people worried about food and clothing, the basic needs of everyday life. He didn’t dismiss their needs. He reordered their priorities.
When God is first, everything else finds its proper place. Before you plan your day, give Him the first few minutes. Seek His heart first, and trust Him to add what you truly need.
prayer: Father, I put You first today. I trust You with everything else.

verse: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end.
title: Hope in the Waiting
message: This promise was given to exiles who would wait seventy years to go home. God didn’t promise them a quick fix. He promised that He had not forgotten them.
If you are in a long season of waiting, God’s thoughts toward you are still thoughts of peace. He has not lost track of your story. Plant your life where you are, and trust Him with the ending.
prayer: Lord, I trust that Your thoughts toward me are good, even while I wait.

verse: I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help. My help cometh from the LORD, which made heaven and earth.
title: Look Up
message: Pilgrims sang this psalm on the way to Jerusalem, a long journey through dangerous hills. Their eyes went to the hills, but their trust went higher, to the One who made them.
Where are your eyes today? On the bills, the headlines, the problem in front of you? Lift them higher. The Maker of heaven and earth is your help, and He does not sleep.
prayer: Lord, I lift my eyes to You. You are my help today.

verse: I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing.
title: Stay Connected
message: A branch doesn’t strain to produce grapes. It simply stays connected to the vine, and life flows through it.

So much of our exhaustion comes from trying to be fruitful while disconnected. Today, abide: whisper a prayer between tasks, read one verse slowly, thank Him out loud. Fruit is His work. Staying close is yours.
prayer: Jesus, I want to abide in You today. Let Your life flow through mine.

verse: And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind.
title: A Renewed Mind
message: We are constantly being shaped by something: feeds, headlines, opinions, fears. Paul says not to be pressed into the world’s mold, but to be transformed from the inside out.

Transformation begins in the mind, and the mind is renewed by truth. What you take in today will shape who you become. Feed your mind with God’s Word, even just one verse, and let Him do the transforming.
prayer: Holy Spirit, renew my mind today. Shape my thoughts with Your truth.

verse: For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God.
title: Not Earned, Received
message: Many of us live as if we’re on spiritual probation, trying to earn God’s approval with good behavior. But salvation was never a wage. It’s a gift.
A gift can only be received, never earned. You can stop performing for God today. He loves you because of His grace, not because of your résumé. Rest in what Jesus has done.
prayer: Thank You, God, for the gift of grace. Help me stop striving and simply receive.

verse: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
title: Light in the Dark
message: David asks two questions, and they’re meant to be answered: Whom shall I fear? No one. Of whom shall I be afraid? No one.
Fear grows in the dark, when we can’t see what’s coming. But God is light. He doesn’t always show us the whole road, but He shows us enough to take the next step. Let Him be your light today.
prayer: Lord, You are my light and my strength. I will not be afraid.

verse: And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.
title: Ordinary Work, Holy Purpose
message: Paul wrote these words to servants doing unseen, unglamorous work. He told them their work mattered, because they were ultimately serving Christ.
Folding laundry, answering emails, changing diapers, closing a sale: none of it is too small for God. Offer your work to Him today. When no one notices, He does.
prayer: Lord, I offer You my work today. Let me do it with my whole heart, for You.

verse: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.
title: Ask for Wisdom
message: Facing a decision you don’t know how to make? James says to ask God, and he describes how God responds: generously, and without scolding you for asking.
God isn’t annoyed by your questions. He is a generous Father who loves to give wisdom. Bring Him the specific decision in front of you today, and expect Him to guide you.
prayer: Father, I need wisdom for ___. Thank You for giving generously.

verse: For the joy of the LORD is your strength.
title: Joy That Strengthens
message: When the people heard God’s law read aloud, they wept over their failures. Nehemiah told them to stop mourning and celebrate, because the joy of the Lord was their strength.
Joy isn’t the absence of sorrow; it’s the presence of God. It’s rooted in who He is, not in how today is going. Ask Him to fill you with His joy, and you’ll find strength you didn’t know you had.
prayer: Lord, fill me with Your joy today, and let it be my strength.

verse: Cast thy burden upon the LORD, and he shall sustain thee: he shall never suffer the righteous to be moved.
title: Let Him Carry It
message: David wrote this psalm after being betrayed by a close friend. He didn’t pretend it didn’t hurt. He took the burden and threw it onto the Lord.
God doesn’t promise to remove every burden immediately. He promises to sustain you while you carry what can’t yet be put down. Name your burden to Him today, and let Him hold you up.
prayer: Lord, I cast this burden on You. Sustain me today.

verse: Behold, I will do a new thing; now it shall spring forth; shall ye not know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert.
title: A Way in the Wilderness
message: God made a way through the Red Sea once. Here He promises something new: not a path through water, but water in the desert.

Maybe your life feels like a wilderness right now, dry and without direction. God specializes in roads where there were none and streams where nothing grows. Look for the new thing He is doing. It may already be springing up.
prayer: Lord, open my eyes to the new thing You’re doing in my wilderness.

verse: Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up.
title: Love Is Patient
message: We often read this chapter at weddings, but Paul wrote it to a church full of conflict and competition. Real love isn’t a feeling; it’s a way of treating people.
Try this today: put your name in place of “charity.” Then ask God for help where it doesn’t fit yet. The love described here is the love Jesus has for you, and He can grow it in you.
prayer: Jesus, make me patient and kind today, the way You are with me.

verse: Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning.
title: Morning Is Coming
message: Some nights feel endless. Grief, worry and pain have a way of making darkness seem permanent. But David reminds us: the night is not the end of the story.
Weeping is real, and God doesn’t rush you through it. But He also promises a morning. If you’re in the night today, hold on. Joy is on its way, as surely as the sunrise.
prayer: Lord, hold me through the night, and bring the morning of joy.

verse: Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.
title: The God of Hope
message: Paul gives God a beautiful name here: the God of hope. Hope isn’t wishful thinking; it’s confident expectation rooted in God’s character.
Notice the order: as we believe, God fills us with joy and peace, and the Holy Spirit makes hope overflow. If your hope feels low today, don’t try to manufacture it. Ask the God of hope to fill you.
prayer: God of hope, fill me with joy and peace as I trust You today.

verse: Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.
title: Let It Shine
message: Jesus didn’t say, “Try to become light.” He said, “You are the light.” If you belong to Him, His light already lives in you.
Light doesn’t have to be loud to be seen. A kind word, a patient answer, a quiet act of generosity can shine in someone’s dark day. Look for one person to shine on today.
prayer: Jesus, let Your light shine through me to someone who needs it today.

verse: He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
title: The Secret Place
message: The secret place is not a building. It is a life lived close to God, returning to Him again and again throughout the day.

Those who dwell there, who make their home in His presence, find themselves sheltered in His shadow. You can step into that secret place right now, in your car, your kitchen or your office. He is there.
prayer: Most High God, I make my home in Your presence today. Shelter me in Your shadow.

verse: If the Son therefore shall make you free, ye shall be free indeed.
title: Free Indeed
message: There are many kinds of chains: habits we can’t break, shame we can’t shake, fears that dictate our choices. Jesus came to set captives free.
His freedom isn’t partial or temporary. It’s “free indeed.” Whatever has been holding you, bring it to Jesus today. The chains may not fall all at once, but the Son has the authority to break them.
prayer: Jesus, You came to set me free. I bring You what binds me today.

verse: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven.
title: Seasons
message: There is a time to plant and a time to harvest, a time to weep and a time to laugh. No season lasts forever, and none is wasted.
If you’re in a hard season, it will not last forever. If you’re in a joyful season, savor it. Ask God what this season is for, and trust that He holds the calendar.
prayer: Lord of every season, help me trust You in this one.

verse: For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
title: Not a Spirit of Fear
message: Timothy was young, timid and leading a difficult church. Paul reminded him where fear doesn’t come from: it isn’t a gift from God.
Instead, God gives power to do what He asks, love to guide how we do it, and a sound mind to stay steady. When fear rises today, name it for what it is, and ask for what God actually gives.
prayer: Lord, replace my fear with Your power, Your love and a sound mind.

verse: Thou wilt shew me the path of life: in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore.
title: Fullness of Joy
message: We search for joy in many places: achievements, relationships, possessions, entertainment. David found it somewhere else: in the presence of God.
Not partial joy. Fullness of joy. Not pleasure for a moment, but forevermore. Take a few minutes today to simply be with God. You may find that what you’ve been looking for was there all along.
prayer: Lord, show me the path of life, and let me find fullness of joy with You.

verse: For with God nothing shall be impossible.
title: Nothing Impossible
message: The angel spoke these words to Mary, a young woman told she would carry the Son of God. Her question was reasonable: How can this be?

God’s answer wasn’t an explanation; it was a reminder of who He is. Whatever seems impossible in your life today, bring it to the One for whom nothing is too hard. Then answer like Mary: “Be it unto me according to thy word.”
prayer: Lord, nothing is impossible for You. I trust You with what seems impossible to me.

verse: And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.
title: Forgiven to Forgive
message: Forgiveness doesn’t mean pretending it didn’t hurt, or that trust is instantly restored. It means releasing the debt, the way God released ours.
Is there someone you need to forgive? Start by remembering how much you’ve been forgiven. Then ask God for help to let go, even if it takes time. Kindness and tenderness often follow forgiveness.
prayer: Father, You have forgiven me so much. Help me forgive ___ today.

verse: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
title: Enough Light for the Next Step
message: Ancient lamps didn’t light up a whole road. They lit just enough ground for the next few steps.

God’s Word often works the same way. It may not reveal your whole future, but it shows you enough to take the next faithful step. Open the Bible today, even for a few verses, and let it light your path.
prayer: Lord, let Your Word light my next step today.

verse: Rejoice evermore. Pray without ceasing. In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.
title: God’s Will for Today
message: We often wonder what God’s will is for our lives. Here Paul makes it plain: rejoice, pray and give thanks, in every circumstance.
Not for every circumstance, but in every one. You can thank God in the middle of a hard day for His presence, His faithfulness, His love. Try it today: one thank-you prayer every hour.
prayer: Lord, teach me to rejoice, pray and give thanks in everything today.

verse: Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.
title: Perfect Peace
message: In Hebrew, “perfect peace” is literally “peace, peace”: peace upon peace. It is promised to the one whose mind is stayed, or leaning, on God.
Our minds will lean on something: our fears, our plans, our phones. When your thoughts start spinning today, gently lean them back on God. Repeat this verse as often as you need it.
prayer: Lord, I lean my mind on You. Keep me in perfect peace.

verse: But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
title: Loved at Your Worst
message: God didn’t wait for us to clean up our lives before He loved us. Christ died for us while we were still sinners.
That means His love doesn’t rise and fall with your performance. On your worst day, you are still loved. On your best day, you are loved just as much. Rest in a love that was proven at the cross.
prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for loving me before I ever loved You.

verse: Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits.
title: Don’t Forget
message: David talks to his own soul and tells it not to forget. We forget so easily: answered prayers, rescues, provision, healing.
Today, make a short list of what God has done for you. Forgiveness, provision, people, protection. Gratitude is memory with a heart toward God, and it strengthens faith for whatever comes next.
prayer: Lord, I bless You today. Help me remember all You’ve done.

verse: And, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world.
title: Always
message: These are the last words of Jesus in Matthew’s Gospel. Before He ascended, He left His disciples with a mission and a promise: I am with you always.
Not some days. Not when you feel spiritual. Always. As you go about your ordinary day, carry this promise with you. You are never on your own.
prayer: Jesus, thank You for being with me always, even today, even now.

verse: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.
title: Faith Sees Further
message: Faith isn’t pretending. It’s trusting God’s promises even before we see them fulfilled. Hebrews 11 lists men and women who lived that way, many of whom died before seeing the full answer.
What are you hoping for that you can’t yet see? Hold it before God today. Faith rests not on what’s visible, but on the One who is faithful.
prayer: Lord, strengthen my faith to trust You for what I can’t yet see.

verse: The LORD is nigh unto all them that call upon him, to all that call upon him in truth.
title: Call on Him
message: You don’t need fancy words or a special place to reach God. He is near to all who call on Him in truth, which means honestly.
Tell Him the truth today: how you really feel, what you really need, what you really fear. He isn’t far away waiting for a perfect prayer. He is near, listening.
prayer: Lord, I call on You honestly today. Thank You for being near.

verse: Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ.
title: He Will Finish It
message: Growth can feel painfully slow. We look at our habits, our temper or our faith and wonder if anything is changing.

Paul is confident, not in us, but in God. The One who started the work in you will finish it. You are a work in progress in the hands of a faithful Craftsman. Be patient with yourself today, as He is patient with you.
prayer: Lord, thank You that You will finish the good work You began in me.

verse: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly.
title: Abundant Life
message: Jesus contrasts Himself with a thief who comes to steal, kill and destroy. He came for the opposite reason: to give life, and life to the full.

Abundant life isn’t a life without problems. It’s a life filled with the presence of Jesus. Look for one thing today that the thief has been stealing, your joy, peace or rest, and ask Jesus to restore it.
prayer: Jesus, You came to give me abundant life. Restore what has been stolen.

verse: The name of the LORD is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe.
title: Run to the Tower
message: In ancient cities, a strong tower was the safest place in a crisis. When enemies came, people didn’t try to fight alone. They ran to the tower.
God’s name, His character and His promises, is that tower. When trouble comes today, don’t stand in the open trying to fix everything. Run to Him in prayer. You are safe there.
prayer: Lord, You are my strong tower. I run to You today.

verse: With men it is impossible, but not with God: for with God all things are possible.
title: Not With God
message: Jesus said these words after His disciples asked, “Who then can be saved?” Salvation itself is something only God can do.

If God can save a human heart, He can handle what you’re facing. Notice the turning point in this verse: “but not with God.” Bring your impossible situation to Him and let those three words change how you see it.
prayer: Lord, what is impossible for me is possible for You. I trust You.

verse: Trust in him at all times; ye people, pour out your heart before him: God is a refuge for us.
title: Pour It Out
message: David doesn’t say tidy up your heart before God. He says pour it out: every fear, frustration and tear.
God is a refuge, a safe place where you can be completely honest. Take five minutes today to pour out your heart to Him, out loud or on paper. You’ll find He can hold all of it.
prayer: Lord, I pour out my heart to You. You are my refuge.

verse: I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me.
title: Christ in Me
message: The Christian life isn’t just trying to be more like Jesus. It’s Jesus living His life through us.
When you feel unable to love, forgive or keep going today, remember that you don’t have to do it alone. Christ lives in you, and He loved you and gave Himself for you. Let Him live through you.
prayer: Jesus, live Your life through me today.

verse: O God, thou art my God; early will I seek thee: my soul thirsteth for thee.
title: Thirsty for God
message: David wrote this psalm in the wilderness of Judah, a dry and weary land. He didn’t first ask for water. He asked for God.
What are you thirsty for today? Approval, rest, answers? Beneath every longing is a soul made for God. Seek Him early, before the noise of the day begins, and let Him satisfy you.
prayer: God, You are my God. My soul thirsts for You. Satisfy me today.

verse: And he that sat upon the throne said, Behold, I make all things new.
title: All Things New
message: At the end of the Bible, God doesn’t make all new things. He makes all things new. He is in the business of restoring what was broken.
Your story isn’t over. Broken relationships, wounded hearts and weary bodies are not beyond His reach. One day He will make everything new. Today, you can taste a little of that hope.
prayer: Lord, You make all things new. Begin with my heart today.
